# Refugio

> A walking-time map of cool refuges for older adults in 45 °C heat, in Culiacán, Hermosillo and Mexicali (Mexico). Built from open data on AWS (Overture Maps, Meta HRSL) and Amazon Location Service. Code: MIT.

## Key figures

- Culiacán: 17,441 of 55,485 older adults (60+), 31.4%, live more than a 15-minute walk from the nearest refuge. 10 proposed public buildings would raise those within 10 minutes from 40.7% to 51.6%.
- Hermosillo: 18,859 of 63,621 older adults (60+), 29.6%, live more than a 15-minute walk from the nearest refuge. 10 proposed public buildings would raise those within 10 minutes from 41.2% to 51.5%.
- Mexicali: 16,242 of 61,403 older adults (60+), 26.5%, live more than a 15-minute walk from the nearest refuge. 10 proposed public buildings would raise those within 10 minutes from 44.1% to 51.9%.

## Evidence

- Against Amazon Location CalculateRoutes in 50 random Culiacán hexagons: median difference 0.5 min, 94% within ±2 minutes, correlation 0.99.
- Amazon Location knows a refuge-type place clearly closer in 10% of those hexagons, so the headline figure is an upper bound.

## Method

- Overture places, streets and boundaries read by bounding box from Amazon S3 with DuckDB; HRSL population (total and 60+) from Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs with rasterio.
- Walking network from Overture road segments, multi-source Dijkstra at 3.6 km/h, results on H3 resolution-10 hexagons.
- Greedy maximum coverage over existing public buildings to propose new refuges.
- Live layer: Amazon Location Geocode, SearchNearby, CalculateIsolines and CalculateRoutes from the user's address (results not stored).
